_meta.why: AI-VEH predicts service due-dates and costs and injects them into the cash-flow forecast as scheduled outflows. It needs a bundled knowledge base of intervals and typical Indian cost ranges per vehicle class so predictions work from the first odometer reading.
_meta.what: Per vehicle class: service intervals (km and months), typical Indian cost ranges (minor units, INR paise), and consumable replacement intervals.
_meta.result: 'Service due ~Aug 20, expect INR 3,000-4,500' style alerts, adjusted by the user's own service-cost history (personal index).
changelog: 2026-07-17 — Created from SRS v1.7 §12. Cost ranges are starter estimates in INR minor units; refined by the user's personal cost index.

2026-09-26 — Issue 10.4 built AI-VEH against this file. The prediction method and the alert thresholds moved out of `_meta`'s prose and into the typed `prediction` and `alerts` blocks below, because an engine cannot consume a sentence: `"30 days / 500 km before due"` had to become two numbers an engine reads and a drift test can check. No interval, cost range or consumable changed. See ADR-0052.
_meta.prediction_note: kmPerMonth = robustSlope(odometer readings, last 12 months). nextService.dueAt = min(lastService.odo + interval_km via kmPerMonth, lastService.date + interval_months). predictedCost adjusted by user's personal cost index.
_meta.alerts_note: The prose these two blocks replaced, kept for the reader: service due '30 days / 500 km before due'; mileage drop '> 15% vs 3-month baseline'; renewal 'insurance / PUC expiry at -30 and -7 days'.

prediction.why: AI-VEH has to turn a handful of odometer readings into a rate, and a rate into a date. Every number that decision needs is here, so changing how far back the app looks, or how many services it wants before it trusts a household's own prices, is an edit to this file rather than to an engine.

notes.slope: Median of the pairwise slopes between readings in the window (Theil-Sen), in whole km per month, so one mistyped odometer reading cannot move the estimate the way a mean would.
notes.personal_index: Median of (this household's service cost / the class midpoint), in basis points, clamped to the floor and ceiling. Below two services there is no index and the KB range is shown as it stands.
notes.default_km_per_month: Zero means 'not enough readings to say' — the engine then predicts on the time interval alone and says so, rather than inventing a distance.

alerts.why: When to speak. A service alert that arrives the day the service is due is useless; one that arrives three months early is noise.
